rule: keep alphanumerics AND '.', '_', '-'; map everything else to '_'; then map the results '', '.' and '..' to '_'. Enumeration is over CODE POINTS, never UTF-16 code units. 'Alphanumeric' follows the host platform's Unicode-aware classification, not ASCII, BOUNDED TO THE BASIC MULTILINGUAL PLANE: a non-Latin BMP order id survives unchanged and is therefore NOT lossy, while every code point above U+FFFF is non-alphanumeric on every host and maps to exactly ONE underscore — the reference's FChar::IsAlnum takes a code unit and cannot classify an astral code point at all, and two hand-maintained Unicode tables would drift. A host that hardcodes [A-Za-z0-9] produces different cache paths for the same order id; so does a host that walks code units.
collisionSuffix: when sanitisation is lossy, append '_' + sha256(utf8(rawOrderId))[:8]

vectors.note: a lossless id gets NO suffix, so existing cache paths are preserved

The rule above says 'alphanumeric' is the platform's Unicode-aware classification, not ASCII. A host that hardcodes [A-Za-z0-9] mangles this to '_____-2026' and derives a DIFFERENT cache path for the same order — the bundle is silently re-downloaded every session. This vector is the only thing that catches it.

vectors.$comment: U+1D7CE MATHEMATICAL BOLD DIGIT ZERO is Unicode category Nd, but classification is BMP-bounded: every host maps a code point above U+FFFF to exactly ONE underscore. A host enumerating UTF-16 code units emits two, and derives a different directory for the same order. Distinctness is not lost - the collision suffix hashes the RAW id.
One non-alphanumeric CODE POINT maps to exactly one underscore. A per-code-unit walk emits two.

vectors.note: path traversal must be neutralised before the string reaches the filesystem
both sanitise to 'a_b'; the hash suffix is what stops one bundle overwriting the other
